# Controller 1 for tools/shift_check.py: battle mode against three CPU
# players (US (NBME)), from power-on with a blank EEPROM.  (frame, BUTTONS word
# in hex, held from that frame on; m64p's BUTTONS: 0x10 START, 0x80 A, the
# stick's X in bits 16-23 and Y in bits 24-31, so 0x00500000 is right,
# 0x00B00000 left, 0x50000000 up and 0xB0000000 down.)
#
# The path, with the overlay loaded (what shift_check.py's checkpoints and
# the emulator show; the screens are told apart by their overlays, the
# menus' text is pictures):
#   from   150: ovl_0B_01
#   from   540: ovl_0A_05
#   from   660: ovl_0B_01
#   from   840: ovl_0B_03
#   from  1290: ovl_17_01
#   START 500, START 600, START 700, stick down 740, A 780, A 930, A 1080, then A from 1230
#
# Why those inputs: the title takes no START in its first ~450 frames;
# the next START (500) goes to the opening logo scene (ovl_0A_05; in jp
# it plays by itself at 360 and START leaves it), another START leaves that
# for the mode menu (ovl_0B_01 again), whose first START wakes it.  Its list
# moves on the stick's Y (the D-pad did nothing): one step down from
# Adventure (file select, ovl_0B_06) is Battle Game (ovl_0B_03), one up
# is ovl_0B_05.  The battle setup (ovl_0B_03) has three screens that A
# takes in turn (the second is a 4x3 grid; B goes back), then the arena
# (ovl_17_01) loads.  The defaults are one human and three CPU players: with
# nothing pressed a match plays itself and ends (ovl_0B_07, the result) once
# the CPUs have killed the idle player; A on the result starts the next.  The
# controllers 2-4 are not plugged in, so player 1 is the only human, and
# there is no setting for four CPU players on one pad that was found.
#
# From 1230 to the end: A every 50 frames (a bomb in the arena, continue
# on the result, the setup's screens when they come back after a set of
# matches) and, from 1560, the stick right, down, left, up in turn every
# 90 frames for 8 (player 1 walks about; started earlier, the stick moved
# the setup's cursors off the path and the first arena came 4000 frames late).
# In the run shift_check.py makes (the random seed pinned), the loads are:
# arena 1290-4320, result 4320-4470, arena to 5940, result to 6120, arena to 11310, result to 11490, arena to 14910, result to 15090, arena to 17220, result to 17370, then the sixth arena.
#
# The script ends at 18000.  A one-frame slip in the shifted build's loads
# (its overlays and main_code are bigger, so some load ends a frame
# later) is not an error, but the game's random draws go different ways
# after it and the states stop being comparable.  Over a long run it
# happens somewhere: with this pattern (found by trying a few) it first
# happens after 17000 in US (NBME) (other patterns slip after 8000-14000).
# The checkpoints are chosen inside the matches and in the result screens
# (a checkpoint can catch the shifted build mid-slip: us at 14000, one
# heap cursor, D_8029F880, differs for a while and then agrees again).
# frames: 1000,2000,3500,4400,5000,6030,8000,10000,11400,12500,13000,15000,16000,17300,17800
#
